subject.title: googlechat: deliver media as a text link when attachment upload is unauthorized (app auth)

question: Should this Google Chat app-auth fallback be allowed to merge with only mocked/source-level proof and narrative production confirmation, or should maintainers require inspectable real app-auth delivery proof?
rationale: The code path is source-reproducible, but this is an external Google Chat delivery and authorization boundary where ClawSweeper cannot independently waive the real-behavior proof gate.

options.title: Require Inspectable Proof
options.body: Ask for redacted logs, terminal/live output, screenshot, recording, or linked artifact showing a real app-auth upload 403 followed by delivered link text before merge.

options.title: Maintainer Waives Proof
options.body: A maintainer may accept source-level proof or provide their own live validation, but the code findings still need repair before merge.

recommendation.title: Require Inspectable Proof
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted logs, terminal/live output, screenshot, recording, or linked artifact showing a real app-auth upload 403 followed by delivered link text before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from original Google Chat commit provenance and prior maintainer-side review context for this channel area.
